overview: An undated State Department list of papers indexes five consular reports from Dairen concerning foreign corporations and commercial activity in the Kwantung Leased Territory during 1934–1936. Three entries follow the Chrysler Automobile Company’s unsuccessful effort to establish a motor-car assembly plant in Dairen and the opposition of the Kwantung Army; two later entries concern a proposed Franco-Japanese development company and the closure of the Dairen office of a British electrical firm because of insufficient business.

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning corporations in Kwantung
subfiles.about: An index identifies five Dairen consular reports from 1934–1936 concerning foreign companies operating or attempting to establish operations in the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists three 1934 reports attributed to Vincent on Chrysler’s proposed automobile assembly plant in Dairen, including the difficulties created by the Kwantung Army and what the consulate regarded as the final settlement of the case. It also lists two 1936 reports by Grummon: one on Lucien Mopiet’s activities in connection with a proposed Franco-Japanese Far Eastern Enterprise Corporation, and another on the General Electric Company of China’s closure of its Dairen office for lack of business. The entries include cross-references to related decimal-file material.

interest: Although only an index sheet, this document maps a small but revealing body of consular reporting on the increasingly constrained environment for Western business in Japanese-controlled Dairen. It connects military opposition to an American automobile venture with later French-Japanese corporate cooperation and the commercial withdrawal of a major British firm. The decimal-file cross-references are especially useful for locating related records and reconstructing cases whose underlying reports are not present here.
